name: Green anarchism
summary: Green anarchism combines the anarchist rejection of the state and hierarchy with an ecological critique, holding that states, capitalism and industrial production drive environmental destruction. It favours stateless, decentralised, bioregional or communal societies, degrowth, direct action and, in some strands, animal liberation. Strands divide mainly over technology and civilization: primitivists want to abandon agriculture and industry, while social ecologists keep reason, cities and technology under democratic control.
scope: Green anarchism (eco-anarchism): the anarchist school that ties environmental crisis to hierarchy, state and capitalism, as Gordon (s5), Price (s6) and EBSCO (s7) define it. It names three main tendencies: Bookchin's social ecology, Næss-style deep ecology (as taken up by Earth First!) and Zerzan's anarcho-primitivism, with Fifth Estate, Green Anarchy and Green Anarchist as its periodicals; the classical roots are Kropotkin and Reclus. Where tendencies disagree (foraging, population, technology, electoral municipal politics) the answer is a split or null. Excluded: Bookchin's later communalism where it breaks with anarchism, Kaczynski and violent offshoots, and eco-socialism or green politics in general. Wikipedia only guided the search.
